Courcol et al. 2015 full text (arXiv 1506.07144, Sect. 5-6, Table 4)
WebSearch
coverage.notes: b (40.0 d warm Neptune, Courcol et al. 2015) is on the confirmed tab. The discovery paper fits b plus a linear drift of -2.34 +/- 0.44 m/s/yr (Table 4) and says it 'might be due to a long-period additional companion' or a magnetic cycle (log R'HK rose over the 2.2 yr span), or an under-corrected SOPHIE zero-point drift; 'additional SOPHIE measurements will help to conclude'. No follow-up paper found. Reported per the owner's ruling that RV-trend-only candidates are ambiguous candidates. Kervella+2022 PMa S/N 1.26 (no astrometric support); Gaia DR3 RUWE 0.90, no NSS; not in GaiaPMEX. NASA pscomppars sy_snum = 2 and exoplanet.eu names the planet 'HD 164595 Ab', but the Systems tab has 1 star; a WebSearch summary mentioned an M-dwarf companion ~683 AU away, which is not in Courcol+2015's text and was not verified (see incidental). Such a wide companion is not offered by anyone as the cause of the trend. The 2015 RATAN-600 'SETI signal' toward this star is not a planet claim.

candidates.tier_reason: Trend-only: 66 SOPHIE RVs over 809 d. The discoverers could not decide between an outer companion, a rising magnetic cycle (activity increased over the run) and an incompletely corrected instrumental zero-point drift. No period, no mass, no follow-up in 11 years, and no Hipparcos-Gaia PMa (Kervella+2022 S/N 1.26). Kept only because the owner's ruling files trend-only signals as ambiguous candidates; on the evidence it is weak.

considered_not_added.name: HD 147513 b
considered_not_added.reason: Already on the confirmed tab. FLAG FOR THE WRITER: NASA pscomppars marks it controversial (pl_controv_flag = 1), and Harada et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 343; SPORES-HWO II, Appendix C.7) find that adding 46 nights of HARPS RVs makes the 528 d signal vanish (only a sub-threshold 504.1 d peak, FAP > 0.01); they say it 'has not since been confirmed by follow-up observations'. exoplanet.eu and OEC still list it Confirmed. Arguably belongs on Unconfirmed as ambiguous.

considered_not_added.name: HD 42618 ~4850 d signal
considered_not_added.reason: Attributed to the stellar magnetic activity cycle by its discoverers (Fulton et al. 2016, Sect. 4.2: period matches the Ca II H&K cycle); CLS Table 7 lists it (4040 d) as a false positive, cause A (activity). Never proposed as a planet.

considered_not_added.name: HD 177565 b
considered_not_added.reason: Already on the confirmed tab. FLAG FOR THE WRITER: single-paper detection that its authors call a 'planet candidate' (Feng et al. 2017, MNRAS 470, 4794, abstract and Sect. 4.5; 68 HARPS points, K = 2.71 m/s); exoplanet.eu status is 'Candidate'. NASA and OEC call it confirmed; no independent confirmation found.

considered_not_added.name: HD 177565 short-period residual signals (e.g. 1.43 d)
considered_not_added.reason: Not a candidate: the 1.43 d peak appears only in a noise model the paper rejects, the residual periodogram after b shows no significant signal, and the conclusion's 'clues for other short period signals' names no period (Feng et al. 2017, Sect. 4.5, 5).

considered_not_added.name: HD 90156 ~14 d residual peak
considered_not_added.reason: Not a candidate: a residual-periodogram peak with FAP 16% about which the discoverers 'can however not yet conclude anything' (Mordasini et al. 2011, A&A 526, A111, Sect. 4.2). No amplitude or mass given; not seen by CLS (Rosenthal et al. 2021 recovers only b).

considered_not_added.name: HD 154088 ~3000 d signal
considered_not_added.reason: Magnetic activity cycle, modelled with a log R'HK term by Unger et al. 2021 (A&A 654, A104, Sect. 5.4). Not a planet claim.

considered_not_added.name: HD 154345 residual 26.2 d and 6.4 yr (2763 d) signals
considered_not_added.reason: Stellar rotation (26.2 d, Prot 27.8 d) and magnetic cycle (6.4 yr), per Giovinazzi et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 52, Sect. VII.6); CLS Table 7 classifies the 2763 d signal as activity (A). Not planet claims.

considered_not_added.name: GJ 3222 c (Ac)
considered_not_added.reason: Brown dwarf: true mass 52.213 (+5.1/-4.9) MJup, P = 1429.8 d, a = 2.39 AU, i = 2.08 deg (Feng et al. 2022, ApJS 262, 21, Table 3 via VizieR J/ApJS/262/21). Above 13 MJup.

considered_not_added.name: GaiaPMEX candidate for HD 21175 (= GJ 3222)
considered_not_added.reason: Kiefer et al. 2025 GaiaPMEX catalogue (VizieR J/A+A/702/A77/tableb1) lists HD 21175 with RUWE 1.214, pRUWE 0.0024, minimum companion mass 3.1 MJup at ~1.97 AU; its NPlNEA = 0 only because NASA carries no Gaia ID for GJ 3222. The astrometric excess is already accounted for by the 52 MJup companion GJ 3222 c (Feng+2022) and the SPHERE stellar companion HD 21175 B (Philipot et al. 2023). Not a new planet candidate.

considered_not_added.name: HD 3651.02 / 54 Psc d (P=31.08 d)
considered_not_added.reason: Refuted: the second planet of the 2:1-resonant alternative to the single eccentric b (Wittenmyer et al. 2013). Subjak et al. 2023 (A&A 671, A10, Sect. 6.1) 'can rule out such a solution' with Lick+Keck+SONG+CARMENES+EXPRES RVs; exoplanet.eu status Retracted. OEC still lists it 'Controversial' (P 31.08 d, 0.09 MJ, a 0.186 AU). If the writer wants every OEC-controversial object logged, it belongs on the Rejected candidates tab.

considered_not_added.name: HD 3651 ~5140 d signal
considered_not_added.reason: Magnetic activity cycle: CLS Table 7 (Rosenthal et al. 2021) false positive, cause A, P = 5140 d; Harada et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 343, App. B.1) recover it at 5157 d and cite the same attribution. Not a planet claim.

considered_not_added.name: 54 Psc c (= HD 3651 B)
considered_not_added.reason: Brown dwarf (T dwarf) companion: exoplanet.eu gives 53 MJup at 476 AU (planet page 54_psc_c--7037, status Confirmed). Above 13 MJup.
